rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The moderate temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Lengthen the gradient with all other settings fixed to test whether the crowded central peaks respond to slope. The current last peak at 7.16 minutes leaves room for a shallower gradient before the time penalty becomes substantial.

Keep the improved gradient and raise temperature to test selectivity at the remaining critical pair, currently R = 1.20. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving room for further slope refinement if needed.

The central peak pattern suggests an elution-order reversal between 40 and 50 °C, so a further temperature increase may reopen the critical pair. Test 55 °C while retaining the slope that already separates the other pairs well.

Slightly steepen the gradient at 55 °C: following the apparent central-pair order reversal, this may open that pair rather than compress it. This also shortens the run while testing whether the neighboring pair retains its resolution margin.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now test a shorter gradient to seek the same full resolution in less time. The pair at R = 1.59 is the likely limiting pair, so retain injection 5 as the fallback.

Trim the gradient window while preserving injection 5’s slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute. This should move the separation earlier while approximately preserving the critical-pair selectivity; the final organic fraction remains above the observed last-peak elution window.

With the maximum-score method secured, test a faster, hotter gradient for an alternative selectivity window. The previously limiting pair may reverse order and separate again, although this is an exploratory test rather than a guaranteed improvement.

The peak widths suggest the limiting pair has reversed order at 60 °C; a steeper gradient may now increase its separation. Shorten tG alone to test that response while checking whether neighboring pairs remain resolved.

The hotter, faster branch is limited by multiple central pairs, so test the low-temperature selectivity range using the original scouting gradient. Injection 5 remains the maximum-score fallback while this run checks for an alternative elution order that could support a shorter fully resolved method.

Trim the unused high-organic portion of injection 5 while preserving its starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope exactly. All peaks previously eluted below approximately 0.58 organic, so this should retain CRF 1.000 with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction opens the reversed central pair at 60 °C, with a slightly shallower slope than injection 8 to protect neighboring separations. Monitor early-peak retention closely; injections 5 and 11 remain proven maximum-score fallbacks.

Raise the starting organic fraction another step to try to open the remaining central pair, while reducing the slope to protect its neighboring separation. Check the first pair carefully because the higher starting strength may compress early peaks.

Return to the successful 55 °C selectivity region and make injection 7’s gradient shallower to recover its limiting pair. This tests whether a trimmed window can achieve full resolution with a larger minimum-resolution margin than injection 5.

Test a narrower gradient window at 40 °C, combining a shallower slope to improve the central separation with a higher starting fraction to reduce retention time. This explores an alternative to the already proven maximum-score methods at 55 °C.

Lengthen injection 15’s gradient by one grid step to improve its sole unresolved pair, currently R = 1.22. The last peak at 8.62 minutes leaves some room to gain full resolution without exceeding the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Test a narrower, shallower gradient at the successful 55 °C temperature to seek larger critical-pair resolution margins while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. The higher starting fraction should offset some of the added retention from the shallower slope.

Refine injection 14 by lowering phi1 one grid step, making the gradient slightly shallower to increase its limiting pair’s resolution margin. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, allowing another maximum-score method with potentially more balanced critical-pair separation.

Test whether modest cooling opens the central pair enough to permit a steeper, faster gradient than the fully resolved 40 °C method. Monitor the other central pairs for temperature-induced crowding; injection 5 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Refine around the fastest proven maximum-score method by lowering the endpoint one step. This slightly shallower gradient should improve the pair previously at R = 1.59, while testing whether the other critical pair remains above 1.5.

Trim the successful gradient to eight programmed minutes while preserving injection 5’s exact slope and starting conditions. The last peak previously eluted at about 0.57 organic, so all peaks should remain within the gradient and retain the maximum CRF.

Test a gradient slope of 0.080 between the fully resolved 0.075 slope and the unsuccessful 0.090 slope. This probes whether the last peak can elute sooner than 7.60 minutes while keeping the limiting pair at R ≥ 1.5.

Refine injection 17 with a slightly shallower slope, targeting its sole unresolved pair at R = 1.41 while preserving the other critical pair’s margin. The predicted last-peak time is about 9.1 minutes, leaving room to reach maximum CRF without a time penalty.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 23 to balance its critical pairs and seek a larger minimum-resolution margin. The last peak is expected near 9.5 minutes, still below the time-penalty threshold; injection 5 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Use a slope between injections 23 and 24 to retain their balanced resolution margins while shortening the programmed gradient and lowering its endpoint. All peaks should elute before 10 minutes; injection 5 remains the fastest proven method achieving the maximum CRF.
